answer: Like a falcon circling a reef, a rotating set of randomly chosen auditor agents inspects newcomers before they can trade. New identities must wander through a probation period, limited to small low-value tasks while building a verifiable work history, and each posts a deposit that auditors slash if they catch duplicated behavior. An attacker must therefore fund, staff, and age every fake identity through real work, so the cost of one Sybil exceeds what it can extract.
